author: emil
text: House rule on the core class, worth keeping in mind since this comes up in review a fair amount: `LLM.__init__` already handles backend resolution, checks the api key env var is present, and normalises the model name. By the time `__call__` has the dataset in hand we have committed to the run and the honest options get a lot worse. So don't let changes to this class push work that belongs in `__init__` down into `__call__`.

author: dario
text: One thing to nail down in the fix: bad config passed to the core class must raise ValueError, same as we already do for an unrecognized backend name or a base_url we can't parse. Callers wrap their setup block in try/except ValueError and branch on it, so anything else (assertion, custom exception, silent clamp to a default) breaks their scripts. If the max output token value is out of range for the model, that's a ValueError at construction, not a warning.

author: emil
text: On the cookbook cost estimate: please don't hand me a hit rate percentage that I have to invert to get anything useful. I want the miss count as a plain int, so I can multiply by price per row and show an actual dollar figure before someone commits to the run. Concretely: add a `misses` field carrying the integer count of rows that missed, not a rate or percentage.
